title: Protection and Safety of Pedestrians Given Challenges Presented by PMDs and E-scooter Users
what_it_is: Protection and Safety of Pedestrians Given Challenges Presented by PMDs and E-scooter Users

sections.label: PMD safety measures and questions
sections.summary: Questions to the Minister for Transport cover additional measures, enforcement, the UL2272 amnesty deadline, registration numbers, education and a possible temporary PMD ban.

sentences.speaker: To ask
sentences.text: the Minister for Transport in light of the challenges in controlling errant PMD users, what additional measures are being considered by LTA to protect the safety of pedestrians and ensure that growth in PMD use does not overwhelm infrastructure capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the Ministry is considering new measures to curb the use of e-scooters, including stronger enforcement and harsher punishments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether the length of the amnesty period ending end-2020 for the use of PMDs which are not compliant with the UL2272 standard should be reviewed in light of the increasing number of fire incidents at homes linked to overcharging of PMD batteries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) to date, how many PMDs have been registered with LTA; (b) how many of them are UL2272-certified; (c) what measures have been taken to educate the registered PMD owners to ride safely and charge their PMDs safely; and (d) whether there are plans to further enhance the safe use of PMDs on public paths.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport in view of the recent spate of fires involving PMDs (a) whether the Ministry can place a temporary ban on the use of PMDs until there are proven solutions for the safer use of PMDs; and (b) whether LTA can bring forward the deadline for all motorised PMDs used on public paths to be certified to the UL2272 standard.

sections.label: PMD fires and deadline
sections.summary: Asks the Minister for Transport whether PMD-related fires spiked in the first half of 2019 and the considerations for not bringing forward the end-2020 non-UL2272 deadline.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether there has been a further spike of PMD-related fires in the first half of 2019 and what are the considerations for not quickly bringing forward the end-2020 deadline banning the use of non-UL2272 devices on public paths.

sections.label: PMD regulation and insurance
sections.summary: Asks the Minister for Transport about regulating PMD purchases and home charging, the certification deadline review timeline, registered PMD numbers, safety certificates and third-party insurance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what further steps will the Ministry be taking to regulate the purchase of safety-compliant PMDs and the charging of PMDs in homes; and (b) what is the timeline for the review of the deadline for the PMD safety certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what is the current number of registered personal mobility devices (PMD); (b) how many of these registered PMDs have a safety certificate; and (c) in view of the increasing number of PMD-related accidents and fire incidents, whether the Ministry will reconsider its position on mandatory third-party insurance for all registered PMDs.
